A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TD-DETR research. All 13 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and supplementary material, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, masked-video experiments, component ablations and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and ablation results, plus architecture, feature-representation, sampling-strategy and context-replacement experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains similarity-based video pairing, context synthesis, temporal differences, dual text cross-attention, weighted fusion and the existing prediction losses. Renamed components and additional architecture evaluations do not establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both original benchmarks remain, but reported highlight-detection evaluation disappears. v2 adds a QVHighlights validation scenario with background clips replaced by another video's context (Section S4.2/Table S5), and extends masked-moment evaluation to Charades-STA (Table 4). These substantially revise evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The QVHighlights comparison adds SnAG, CG-DETR, UVCOM and BAM-DETR; Charades-STA adds SnAG, CG-DETR and BAM-DETR. The masked-video comparison replaces v1's untrained/QD-DETR controls with comparisons involving QD-DETR, CG-DETR and BAM-DETR and their augmented variants.

E3.justification: Spurious evaluation changes from zero-valued to random-valued masks and revises the reported metrics. QVHighlights encoder/decoder depth changes from two to three layers and training from 220 to 200 epochs. Charades-STA learning rate changes from 2e-4 to 1e-4, with decay every 40 rather than 30 epochs; beta changes from 0.5 to 0.7. Architecture and InternVideo2 experiments introduce additional configurations.

E4.justification: v2 extends component ablations to Charades-STA and spurious metrics, revises sensitivity studies, and adds random-versus-similarity sampling, architecture transfer, feature-representation and context-replacement analyses (Tables 4–5 and S3–S5). New qualitative cases replace and expand v1's masked-video example.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies three-run averaging for the standard Charades-STA results in Table 2. Three-run averaging and standard deviations for QVHighlights were already reported. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of an increased run count.

E6.justification: Reported TD-DETR QVHighlights test average mAP changes from 44.65 to 46.69, and Charades-STA R1@0.7 from 36.18 to 40.35. Training settings also change, so these are not isolated same-setting gains. Numerous architecture, robustness and feature results are added; highlight-detection and unmasked gIoU results are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical constructions for similarity, token differences, attention, fusion, matching and losses are retained. Equation revisions primarily concern notation and exposition; neither version supplies new theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim to address query-background spurious correlations through the same two strategies and achieve state-of-the-art moment retrieval on both benchmarks. v2 foregrounds architectural generalization, but v1 already claimed compatibility with any moment-retrieval network in Section 2.2.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's assertion that the masking results confirm correct causal inference, emphasizing mitigation and generalization instead. It adds interpretations of similarity-based sampling and a claimed failure condition at beta=0 caused by missing object cues, although Table S2 does not contain that setting.

D1.justification: v2 removes the explicit dataset-specific loss-weight lists, adds disclosure that SnAG uses official code with SlowFast+CLIP features, and specifies InternVideo2 for additional experiments. Both versions promise future code release; v2 additionally promises the modified validation set, without providing access.

R1.justification: Citations and discussion add SnAG/hybrid grounding, CG-DETR, UVCOM, InternVideo2 and causal VQA while pruning older architectural examples. Section 2 further distinguishes spatial biases from video-context associations, while retaining the central novelty positioning around spurious correlations in moment retrieval.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten, method explanations are condensed, and experimental narration is reorganized into separate standard, spurious and generalization sections. Supplementary material is reorganized into S1–S5. The title, author block and component terminology also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives a new example and standard-versus-spurious mAP plot; architecture diagrams are revised, and Figure 4 is replaced with timestamped predictions and IoUs. Comparison and ablation tables change structure substantially, while Table 5, Tables S3–S5 and Figures S1–S2 add new displays.

improvement.justification: Stronger baselines and the context-replacement, sampling and transfer experiments provide better support for the central robustness claim than v1's narrower evaluation. However, v2 introduces impossible Charades-STA recall orderings in Table 4, misidentifies Table 3 metrics in Section 4.3, and removes explicit loss weights. These reporting and reproducibility defects limit the net quality gain.
